title: Descent of a geometric cohomological dimension bound
statement:
Let $X$ be a finite-type
scheme over a field $K$, and let $\overline K$ be an algebraic
closure. If $\operatorname{cd}_{\rm tor}(K)\leq c$ and
$\operatorname{cd}_{\rm tor}(X_{\overline K})\leq e$, then
$\operatorname{cd}_{\rm tor}(X)\leq c+e$, using
[def-sc-etale-torsion-cd].

proof.text: Put $S=\operatorname{Spec}K$ and $f:X\to S$. Finite type gives quasi-compactness. The field $K$ is Noetherian (its only ideals are $0$ and $K$); every affine finite-type chart of $X$ has Noetherian coordinate ring by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian]. Thus $X$ is locally Noetherian, and [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated] makes intersections of affine opens quasi-compact. Since the base is affine, this makes $f$ quasi-separated as well. Hence $f$ and $X$ are qcqs; the stalk formula and the filtered-colimit theorem apply without a separatedness assumption.

Choose the geometric point $\bar s:\operatorname{Spec}\overline K\to S$, and let $K^{\rm sep}\subset\overline K$ be the relative separable closure of [def-weil-pbc-relative-separable-closure]. This is a separably closed separable algebraic extension of $K$. Let $C$ be the coordinate ring of $S_{(\bar s)}$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-chart-maximal-ideal] with the identity chart $\operatorname{Spec}K\to S$: the maximal ideal of $C$ is the extension of the unique prime $(0)$, hence is zero. By [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-pointed-map] there is a surjection $\psi:C\to K^{\rm sep}$ with this kernel, hence an isomorphism. If the chosen representative of the identity pointed neighbourhood is $(V,\bar v)$, let $a:V\xrightarrow{\sim}S$ be its pointed isomorphism over $S$, so $a\circ\bar v=\bar s$. By [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-structural-map], $a\circ\pi_V=\operatorname{Spec}\rho$. Compose the pointed-map equality for $V$ with $a$; on coordinate rings it says $j\circ\psi\circ\rho=j_K$, where $j:K^{\rm sep}\hookrightarrow\overline K$ and $j_K:K\hookrightarrow\overline K$ are the chosen embeddings. Since $j$ is injective, $\psi\circ\rho$ is the given inclusion $K\hookrightarrow K^{\rm sep}$; thus the isomorphism is over $K$. Consequently $S_{(\bar s)}\cong\operatorname{Spec}K^{\rm sep}$ over $S$.

source.place: Tag 04HX (lemma-describe-etale-local-ring), together with Algebra Tag 04GP (lemma-strict-henselization), properties (4) and (5)

proof.text: Let $F$ be an abelian etale sheaf on $X$ annihilated by a positive integer $n$. The extension $\overline K/K^{\rm sep}$ is algebraic, and [lem-pc-kbar-pure-insep] makes it purely inseparable. The homeomorphism assertion [lem-pc-homeo-pure-insep], applied to every $K^{\rm sep}$-scheme $T$, shows that $T_{\overline K}\to T$ is a homeomorphism. Every base change of $u:X_{\overline K}\to X_{K^{\rm sep}}$ has this form, so $u$ is a universal homeomorphism. Apply [thm-weil-pbc-universal-homeomorphism-invariance] to obtain $H^q(X_{K^{\rm sep}},F|_{X_{K^{\rm sep}}})\cong H^q(X_{\overline K},F|_{X_{\overline K}})$. Pullback of the equation $n\,\mathrm{id}_F=0$ gives the same equation on the restricted sheaf, so every local section is killed by the same positive integer $n$. It is therefore torsion in the local-section sense on the small etale site required by the current [def-sc-etale-torsion-cd]. By [def-sc-etale-torsion-cd] and the assumed geometric bound, these groups vanish for $q>e$.

source.place: Tag 03SI (proposition-topological-invariance); Fields Tag 030K (lemma-separable-first), as in lemma-smooth-base-change-separably-closed

proof.text: For every $q\geq0$, apply [prop-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-stalk-formula] to $f,F,\bar s$ and step 2 to identify $(R^qf_*F)_{\bar s}$ with $H^q(X_{K^{\rm sep}},F|)$. For $q>e$ this is zero by step 3. The equivalence [lem-exc-abelian-sheaves-gmodules] detects zero objects from this single fixed geometric stalk, so $R^qf_*F=0$ for $q>e$. Moreover, the same stalk group is killed by $n$: the additive cohomology functor sends $n\,\mathrm{id}_{F|}=0$ to $n\,\mathrm{id}_{H^q}=0$. Faithfulness of the stalk equivalence therefore gives $n\,\mathrm{id}_{R^qf_*F}=0$ for every $q$. In particular every $R^qf_*F$ is torsion.

Apply [thm-sp-grothendieck] to $f_*$ followed by $\Gamma(S,-)$. The source and middle categories are Grothendieck abelian by [lem-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves-grothendieck]. Direct image is additive and left exact by [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. Global sections is additive and left exact: as sections at the terminal object [def-weil-pbc-global-sections-functor], it preserves kernels and finite products, both computed sectionwise. The category of abelian groups is Grothendieck (small colimits are quotients of direct sums by the diagram relations, filtered colimits of exact sequences are exact elementwise, and $\mathbf Z$ is a generator). By [lem-weil-pbc-direct-image-preserves-injectives], $f_*I$ is injective for injective $I$; [lemma-weil-pbc-leray-acyclicity](1) makes it $\Gamma(S,-)$-acyclic. Finally the section formula for direct image gives $\Gamma(S,f_*F)=\Gamma(X,F)$. The resulting first-quadrant spectral sequence is $E_2^{p,q}=H^p(S,R^qf_*F)\Rightarrow H^{p+q}(X,F)$, with the cohomology identification of [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology].

source.place: Tag 0732 (lemma-Leray), using Tag 0730 (lemma-pushforward-injective-flat) and Derived Categories Tag 015N (lemma-grothendieck-spectral-sequence)

proof.text: By step 4, $E_2^{p,q}=0$ when $q>e$. For $p>c$, it is zero by the field bound [def-sc-etale-torsion-cd], since step 4 proves $n\,\mathrm{id}_{R^qf_*F}=0$, hence every local section is locally killed by a positive integer, as the current definition requires. The field notation means ordinary derived-section cohomology on the small etale site of $S=\operatorname{Spec}K$. If $t>c+e$ and $p+q=t$, at least one of $p>c$ and $q>e$ holds. Thus every $E_2$ term of total degree $t$ is zero, and every later term there remains zero, being the cohomology of a page with zero term at that position. Convergence of [thm-sp-grothendieck], in the sense of [def-sp-convergence], identifies the graded pieces of the abutment filtration with $E_\infty^{p,t-p}=0$. For $p<0$ and $p>t$, first-quadrantness gives zero graded pieces, so the filtration is constant for $p\leq0$ and for $p\geq t+1$. Exhaustiveness in [def-sp-convergence] makes its first constant value $F^0H^t=H^t$, and separatedness makes its last constant value $F^{t+1}H^t=0$. The remaining successive quotients are zero as well; descending induction from $F^{t+1}=0$ to $F^0$ gives $H^t(X,F)=0$. This proves the required bound for every sheaf killed by some positive integer.

source.place: Tag 015N (lemma-grothendieck-spectral-sequence): finite filtration on each abutment; convergence conventions Tag 012U

proof.text: Now let $F$ be any torsion abelian sheaf on the small etale site of $X$, meaning that every local section is locally killed by a positive integer, with no uniform annihilator assumed, exactly as in the current [def-sc-etale-torsion-cd]. By [lemma-weil-pbc-torsion-filtered-union], $F=\varinjlim_{n\in(\mathbf N_{>0},\mid)}F[n]$, with $F[n]=\ker(n:F\to F)$ and inclusion transition maps; the index is filtered by common multiples. Each $F[n]$ is killed by $n$, so step 6 gives $H^t(X,F[n])=0$ for $t>c+e$. Since $X$ is qcqs by step 1, [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-filtered-colimit] identifies $H^t(X,F)$ with $\varinjlim_n H^t(X,F[n])=0$. The definition [def-sc-etale-torsion-cd] now gives $\operatorname{cd}_{\rm tor}(X)\leq c+e$.
